facts.statement: Primobucco is an extinct genus of birds classified in its own family, Primobucconidae.
facts.quote: Primobucco is an extinct genus of bird placed in its own family, Primobucconidae.

facts.statement: The genus was first described in 1970 by American paleo-ornithologist Pierce Brodkorb based on a fossil right wing.
facts.quote: It was initially described by American paleo-ornithologist Pierce Brodkorb in 1970, from a fossil right wing

facts.statement: The type species, Primobucco mcgrewi, lived in North America during the Lower Eocene.
facts.quote: The type species, Primobucco mcgrewi, lived during the Lower Eocene of North America.

facts.statement: Further fossils discovered in 2010 suggest that Primobucco was an early type of roller rather than an early puffbird.
facts.quote: However, the discovery of a further 12 fossils in 2010 indicate that it is instead an early type of roller.

facts.statement: Primobucco lived between 56 and 41.03 million years ago, spanning the Ypresian to Lutetian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Lutetian (56 to 41.03 million years ago)

facts.statement: Seeds found in the digestive tracts of two specimens suggest that Primobucco was more omnivorous than modern rollers, which are exclusively predatory.
facts.quote: Two specimens of P. frugilegus have been found with seeds in the area of their digestive tract, which suggests that these birds were more omnivorous than the exclusively predaceous modern rollers.

facts.statement: Primobucco belongs to the parent group Coracii.
